title: A size-extensive quantum advantage in thermodynamic performance

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a thermodynamic machine whose quantum properties produce a measurable performance advantage that persists as the number of working units increases. Coherence, entanglement or quantum statistics would improve net delivered power, conversion efficiency or steadiness under a clearly defined comparison with classical machines. The advantage would survive accounting for the resources needed to prepare reservoirs, generate quantum states, operate controls, couple components and reset the machine, while useful work reaches a measured load.

Conceptual clarification: size refers to the number of working units, rather than the number of cycles completed by one unit. A larger machine must retain a meaningful relative advantage while producing useful total output. Evidence from two finite sizes would establish an initial scaling result over that range; it would not establish asymptotic extensivity or superiority over every possible classical machine. The supplied single-ion and single-transmon experiments provide foundations for this target without demonstrating the full capability.

significance.text: Significance assessment: a reproducible quantum advantage that survives increasing working-unit count and complete resource accounting would establish a new basis for thermodynamic machine design. Its immediate consequence would be experimentally validated performance principles for the demonstrated machine class: which quantum resources help, under which operating conditions, and whether their benefit exceeds their preparation and control costs. This would extend the few-body operating principles demonstrated in the supplied experiments into a capability with evidence of scalability.

The potential benefit spans several distinct objectives. More net power means delivering useful work faster; higher efficiency means converting a greater fraction of the accounted energy input into work; greater steadiness means reducing output fluctuations under specified operating conditions. These gains need not occur together. A claim about one metric must retain the conditions and tradeoffs under which it was measured, rather than imply simultaneous improvement in all three.

Extensions to refrigerators and heat pumps are plausible because they share quantum control and energy-exchange mechanisms with engines; the single-ion paper explicitly anticipates relevance to these devices. Benefits for clocks, sensors and practical energy technology remain conditional possibilities requiring device-specific mechanisms and demonstrations. A single-ion advantage over a restricted classical comparator does not by itself establish scalable energy technology. The superconducting experiment also describes its achieved power and efficiency as low and without current practical applications.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability within the supplied experimental record is an integrated demonstration of persistent quantum performance advantage as working-unit count grows, with complete resource accounting and verified work delivery. The single-ion experiment measures energy transferred to an oscillator battery, while the superconducting experiment derives thermodynamic output from measured qubit populations and frequencies. Neither reviewed experiment demonstrates scaling with the number of working units. The supplied record does not establish whether another experiment has achieved the broader target elsewhere in the field.

A central accounting barrier is determining whether a performance gain remains after the resources enabling it are included. The single-ion study discusses the cost of shortcut-to-adiabaticity control and notes that this cost lacks a unique definition. A convincing larger machine therefore needs an explicit accounting boundary covering reservoir preparation, quantum-state preparation, control, coupling and reset, with consistent treatment of the classical benchmark. The supplied evidence does not establish the earlier general assertion that including coherence costs restores several classical bounds.

Engineering synthesis: increasing the number of working units requires maintaining the relevant quantum dynamics while coordinating controls, reservoir contacts and energy extraction. Noise, unwanted interactions, uneven working units and control overhead could erase a small-machine advantage. Output measurement must also distinguish energy accumulated in a battery from the useful work deliverable through a specified load. Where strong coupling matters, consistent allocation of interaction energy could support fair accounting, but that accounting framework would be an enabling method rather than the target capability itself.

Benchmarking synthesis: a comparison must specify the classical resources and protocols allowed under matched bath conditions, couplings and cycle duration. Beating the strongest classical protocol identified by the experimenters supports a bounded advantage claim. Establishing superiority over an entire allowed classical class would additionally require a justified bound or exhaustive characterization of that class; the single-ion comparison with energy-diagonal dynamics does not supply such a universal guarantee.

current_state.text: Hou, Yao, Zhao and coauthors reported a single trapped-ion engine coupled to a harmonic-oscillator battery in Nature Communications 16, 5127, published on 2 June 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-60179-5. Oscillations of work output with cycle count reveal intercycle quantum coherence. The classical comparator is constrained so that the engine and battery remain diagonal in their energy bases; the absence of intercycle coherence belongs to that comparator, rather than to the demonstrated quantum engine. The reported quantum output exceeds this restricted comparator.

In the same experiment, the reported relative power enhancement from counterdiabatic shortcut driving ranges from 7.4(17.5)% to 33.2(20.0)%, depending on cycle time. These values compare shortcut-assisted power with unassisted power at fixed cycle count. They do not quantify advantage over every classical protocol, and the reported uncertainties are substantial. Conversion efficiency was not measured. The battery measurement uses its average phonon number after a selected number of Otto cycles to determine transferred energy, providing experimental output evidence without establishing a scalable machine delivering work through a separately characterized practical load.

Uusnäkki, Mörstedt, Teixeira, Rasola and Möttönen demonstrated a single-transmon superconducting Otto engine. The supplied record associates arXiv:2502.20143 with a 2026 Nature Communications journal article, DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-72651-x. The retained evidence reviewed was matching full journal XML obtained through an alternative repository, rather than a verified extraction of the linked arXiv rendering. Single-shot qubit measurements track state evolution; output power and efficiency are derived from measured populations and transition frequencies and agree with corresponding simulations. Positive output power is demonstrated in that measurement framework, while quantum advantage is presented as a future exploration. There is no separately measured output load or demonstration of scaling with working-unit count in the reviewed account.

The earlier research also cites Campbell and coauthors' Roadmap on quantum thermodynamics, attributed to Quantum Science and Technology 11, 012501, dated 29 January 2026, DOI 10.1088/2058-9565/ae1e27, and attributes to it uncertainty about a real advantage from coherent dynamics. No source text for that publication was captured in the supplied review, so its bibliographic details and attributed assessment remain unverified here. Likewise, the research attributes increased distillable work from non-Markovian processes to Zambon and Adesso, Physical Review Letters 134, 200401, dated 20 May 2025, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.200401; that source was not captured. If confirmed, such a formal resource result would concern work extraction under specified process assumptions and would still require an additional experimental scaling demonstration to establish this innovation.

Unverified research item: the earlier research attributes an NMR spin Otto engine operating at approximately 42% efficiency against its own 44% limit to Peterson and coauthors, Physical Review Letters 123, 240601, dated 9 December 2019, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.240601. No source text or source URL for that paper was supplied. The efficiency figures, date and interpretation therefore remain unresolved rather than established or refuted.

The supplied review had complete, untruncated text for the two main experimental publications, plus single-ion supplementary material. Its quantitative assessment relies on text and captions; plotted figures were not independently inspected, and no independent numerical reanalysis was performed. The supplied freshness record contains no bounded search establishing field-wide status as of 1 November 2026. The documented experiments therefore support dated, limited achievements without resolving whether the full target remains open across the field.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed initial scaling milestone: test two machine sizes differing in working-unit count by at least a factor of four, with at least ten coupled working units in the larger machine. Use matched bath conditions and cycle duration, and state how couplings and other resource constraints are matched as size changes. Report net delivered power, conversion efficiency and power variance, with uncertainties and a specified averaging interval. Ten units and fourfold size separation are proposed thresholds for an informative first demonstration, not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Test fourfold-separated sizes with at least ten coupled units in larger machine

completion_criteria.text: Proposed comparison requirement: define the allowed classical resources and protocols before interpreting the result, account for reservoir preparation, quantum-state preparation, control, coupling and reset, and compare with the strongest classical protocol identified within that class. Prespecify at least one success metric. Require its relative improvement to increase with machine size or remain above 50% at the larger size. Improvement means higher net power or efficiency, or lower power variance at matched mean power. The experiment must define the normalization, comparator value and statistical interpretation; the proposed 50% threshold is an author-selected milestone.
completion_criteria.label: Resource-accounted classical improvement increases with size or exceeds 50% at larger size

completion_criteria.text: Proposed work-delivery and reproducibility requirement: verify useful output through a measured load or a battery with characterized work extraction, including losses and measurement uncertainty. Document the load, operating point, duty cycle, usable output and energy-accounting boundary sufficiently for independent reproduction. Repeat the result across devices and operating runs, and establish that the prespecified advantage persists within the reported uncertainty rather than appearing only at an isolated favorable setting.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce measured useful output and prespecified advantage across devices and runs

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation boundary: report exactly which sizes, protocols and operating conditions demonstrate an advantage. Two finite sizes provide initial scaling evidence; additional sizes and a justified scaling model would strengthen the case for persistent behavior. A bounded experimental benchmark does not establish superiority over every classical engine. Practical usefulness would require separate evidence that output, stability, lifetime and supporting infrastructure meet the demands of a specified application.
completion_criteria.label: Report experimental boundaries and limits of demonstrated quantum advantage

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: THR-02, Useful heat engines that are simultaneously efficient, powerful, and steady, has the closest performance overlap. THR-02 concerns the joint achievement of those properties; THR-05 concerns an advantage attributable to quantum resources that survives scaling and fair comparison. A THR-05 demonstration could improve one metric while leaving important tradeoffs in the others, so neither entry subsumes the other.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-03, General-purpose digital computation near the Landauer scale, and THR-08, Equilibrium sampling computers operating near thermal energy per sample, share the need to account for preparation, control and reset resources. Their outputs are computations or samples. THR-05 concerns thermodynamic machine performance and delivered work; efficient computation alone would not demonstrate this engine capability.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-01, A computable thermodynamic potential for far-from-equilibrium continuum transport, and THR-11, Operational temperature and entropy for far-from-equilibrium matter, concern predictive or operational thermodynamic descriptions. Such descriptions could help define reservoirs and compare energy flows in difficult operating regimes. Establishing them would remain distinct from demonstrating a quantum machine with a persistent performance advantage.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-04, Bulk electronic heat–charge decoupling sufficient for engine-class solid-state conversion, and THR-06, A single-absorber solar converter that uses non-thermal carriers to pass the detailed-balance limit, target particular conversion mechanisms. A converter based on either mechanism might also be tested for quantum thermodynamic advantage, but improved solid-state conversion or performance beyond a specified solar limit does not automatically establish THR-05's scaling and classical-benchmark requirements.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-07, Synthetic chemomechanical engines whose efficiency approaches biological molecular motors, overlaps through useful work delivery by small engines. THR-09, A thermodynamic design theory of self-replicators, confirmed by a predicted non-biological replicator, and THR-12, Predictive thermodynamic design of far-from-equilibrium chemical reaction networks, overlap through controlled nonequilibrium energy use. Their defining achievements concern molecular mechanics, replication or reaction-network prediction, respectively; they do not require a scalable quantum advantage.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-10, A laboratory measurement of the Unruh temperature, concerns a specific thermodynamic measurement associated with acceleration. Even if quantum detectors or reservoir concepts connect the subjects, observing that temperature would not demonstrate a machine-performance advantage. THR-05 also intersects quantum control, many-body physics, quantum batteries and superconducting circuits: these can supply mechanisms, working media or output storage, while the defining achievement remains net thermodynamic performance under scaling.

change_log.change: Preserved THR-05 and its title while defining the target through net performance, working-unit count and verified output.
change_log.reason: The concept is coherent; weaknesses in individual supporting assertions do not justify deleting or replacing it.

change_log.change: Corrected the single-ion coherence description and identified the energy-diagonal classical comparator.
change_log.reason: The reviewed experiment reports intercycle quantum coherence; absence of that coherence characterizes the comparator.

change_log.change: Replaced the ambiguous approximately 33% work advantage with the reported 7.4(17.5)% to 33.2(20.0)% shortcut-assisted power enhancement and its actual denominator.
change_log.reason: The reported values compare assisted and unassisted power, carry substantial uncertainty and do not quantify universal classical advantage.

change_log.change: Added the oscillator-battery measurement, absence of measured single-ion conversion efficiency, and population-based superconducting output inference.
change_log.reason: These distinctions establish what was measured and prevent proof-of-concept output from being conflated with scalable load delivery.

change_log.change: Replaced the superconducting paper's unverified quotation with a paraphrase and explained the journal-XML evidence associated with the supplied arXiv URL.
change_log.reason: The candidate quotation was absent from the retained journal text, while the journal identity and experimental result were verified in the supplied review.

change_log.change: Retained the Roadmap, Peterson and Zambon–Adesso research items with explicit evidence limitations.
change_log.reason: Their detailed assertions were not verified from supplied source texts; missing evidence does not establish that the publications or results are false.

change_log.change: Reframed the broad coherence-cost and restored-classical-bounds assertion as an unresolved accounting question.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports attention to shortcut-control costs but does not establish the original general claim.

change_log.change: Separated immediate scientific consequences from conditional applications to refrigerators, clocks, sensors and practical energy technology.
change_log.reason: The latter require additional mechanisms and device-specific demonstrations.

change_log.change: Clarified benchmark scope, variance direction, uncertainty, reproducibility and proposed numerical milestones.
change_log.reason: An identified classical protocol cannot certify universal superiority, and two finite sizes cannot establish asymptotic extensivity.

change_log.change: Added distinctions across the supplied concept roster and separated enabling strong-coupling accounting from the target capability.
change_log.reason: Related thermodynamic goals and methods overlap without being interchangeable achievements.

change_log.change: Preserved figure-inspection, numerical-reanalysis and freshness limitations.
change_log.reason: The final record must not imply broader inspection or field-wide coverage than the supplied review provides.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish field-wide openness or completion of the target as of 1 November 2026.
The Roadmap's bibliographic details and attributed assessment remain unverified because its source text was not captured.
The Peterson publication's reported 42% efficiency, 44% limit, date and interpretation remain unverified; no source URL was supplied.
The Zambon–Adesso non-Markovian work-distillation result remains unverified from source text, including its assumptions and scope.
A complete resource-accounting convention, including shortcut-control costs and any relevant strong-coupling interaction energy, remains to be specified.
The allowed classical comparison class and any bound supporting class-wide superiority remain to be defined.
The proposed numerical milestones need an operational definition of improvement and statistical confidence; they are not consensus standards.
The relation between measured battery energy and useful extracted work requires a specified load and extraction protocol.
Persistence beyond a finite tested size range and practical benefits for refrigerators, clocks, sensors or energy technology require additional demonstrations.
